reason: The hypothesis makes specific mechanistic claims about surface segregation, cohesive energy reduction, and premelting acceleration in HEA nanoparticles, but cites no prior evidence whatsoever to support these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the specific behavior of multi-component HEA nanoparticles under these conditions, so citations are required.
premises: Surface segregation of lower-melting-point constituents occurs in HEA nanoparticles upon annealing
Surface segregation reduces local cohesive energy at the nanoparticle surface
Reduced surface cohesive energy accelerates the onset of premelting
Uniformly distributed HEA nanoparticles serve as a valid baseline without surface segregation
In-situ heating TEM can distinguish premelting onset differences due to surface segregation
